approach: Add two optional keys, `planner_revision_model` and `planner_revision_effort`, to `Models` in config.rs. A new `Models::planner_revision_setting(model, effort)` uses each key only when it is set and not weaker than the current planner value. Effort is ranked by position in `EFFORT_LEVELS`. The model is ranked by position in `producer_allowed`, which is documented as weakest first. A key that is earlier in the list than the current model, or whose value cannot be ranked, is ignored on its own. In `planning_round` a call is a revision call when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. That covers a critic revise and a mechanical plan-rule revision, and leaves round 1 (including a seeded first call) alone. A revision call takes its model from the new function and sets `spec.effort` after `agent_spec`, as producer.rs:338 does, and the UI line shows the effort. The recorded invocation carries both values. The `planner_revision_model` membership check goes after the OLY-B-SET-02 family loop (finding 1, option a), so the existing family tests keep their error. `reading_inputs` clears both keys like `job_plan`. athena.toml, CHANGELOG, D179 and the OLY-A-11 spec text state the effective setting. `producer_setting` and `hard_producer_*` are not read on the planner path.

decisions.choice: Dedicated keys planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort, never derived from hard_producer_*.
decisions.reason: In this repo hard_producer_model is claude-sonnet-5-5 and hard_producer_effort is high (athena.toml:25-26). The planner of a hard job already runs on the hard producer model (reading.rs:869-886) at verifier_effort, which is high (config.rs:835, athena.toml:21). Reusing hard_producer_* would change nothing here, and in another config it could lower the setting.

rejected.option: Reuse hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort via producer_setting
rejected.why: No effect here (same model, same effort), it can lower the planner setting, and the request forbids it.

rejected.option: A code-side bump of effort by one level on revision
rejected.why: It hides the rule from athena.toml and gives the owner no value to set.

decisions.choice: Judge 'not weaker' in code: effort by index in EFFORT_LEVELS (config.rs:336-337), model by index in producer_allowed read as weakest first. A part that would lower the value, or cannot be ranked, is ignored on its own. The field doc comment and the athena.toml comment both say: a key is ignored whenever it sits earlier in producer_allowed than the current model.
decisions.reason: The rule is enforced by mechanism and tested. Answers finding 2: the order is documented in both places, and a config.rs table row with a reversed producer_allowed pins the behavior under reordering, not just this repo's order.

rejected.option: Ignore both keys together when either would lower the setting
rejected.why: The reading says only that part falls back.

rejected.option: Hard-code a family order haiku < sonnet < opus
rejected.why: Brittle on version bumps; the allowed list already carries the order.

rejected.option: Add a validation that producer_allowed is ordered
rejected.why: No machine-readable strength exists to check it against; it would invent a ranking.

decisions.reason: It is exactly a call after a critic revise (round advances in plan_round, planning.rs:41) or after a mechanical revision (passes counted, planning.rs:68-70). A seeded first call has `revision` Some but is neither, so testing `revision.is_some()` would wrongly escalate it.

rejected.why: A seeded retry's first call (planning.rs:39-40, 48-52) would escalate, against 'round 1 is unchanged'.

decisions.choice: Set `spec.effort` after `agent_spec`, as producer.rs:338-340 does, instead of changing `effort_for` or `agent_spec`.
decisions.reason: `effort_for(Role::Planner)` stays the baseline and no other caller of `agent_spec` (about 14 parameters, many callers) changes.

rejected.option: Add a revision flag to agent_spec
rejected.why: Many callers; the override is local to the planner.

decisions.reason: A planner-only setting changes neither what the reader sees nor the scope of a job (D38). Without the reset, adding the keys to athena.toml changes the config digest and stales stored readings. The same rule is what the steward's `reread_changed_scope` (steward.rs:361-371) and the gate's dispatched/accepted comparison (athena-gate/src/jobs.rs:466-468) rely on: a digest change is a settings change, and a planner-only key must not count as one, the same as [job_plan]. Fields are skipped in serialization when None, so existing digests hold.

rejected.option: Leave the keys in the digest
rejected.why: Setting them would invalidate every stored reading and trigger settings-change re-reads for no reason.

decisions.choice: Place the `planner_revision_model` membership check (ConfigError::PlannerRevisionNotAllowed) after the OLY-B-SET-02 family loop (config.rs:691-695) in `validate`. The effort key joins the existing effort array (config.rs:665-670), which runs earlier.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1 with option (a). `roles_without_sonnet_are_refused` (config.rs:1393-1413) rewrites producer_allowed to haiku only, but REPO_CONFIG will hold planner_revision_model = claude-sonnet-5-5. With the check after the family loop, that parse still returns ModelFamily('sonnet') first, so the test and the other `family_refused` tests pass unedited. A valid config is still refused for a stray model.

rejected.option: Put the check beside the hard_producer_model check at config.rs:677-681 and edit the test to rewrite planner_revision_model
rejected.why: Option (b): it edits an existing test, and every future family test would need the same rewrite.

decisions.choice: Keep a short drain.rs test, named `planner_revision_takes_effect_in_the_repository_config`, that parses `common::test_config()`.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 and the deliverables allow drain.rs. It checks the athena.toml as it is, so deleting the entry fails it. What the owner sees on each round is asserted by the core test's `Lines` check. The name matches the `planner_revision` filter and is short (finding 4).

rejected.option: Drop drain.rs and test only over REPO_CONFIG in config.rs
rejected.why: REPO_CONFIG is a copy; only drain.rs reads the real athena.toml through test_config(). The deliverable list also names drain.rs.

risks.risk: The model ordering is read from producer_allowed list order, and nothing in code enforces it. A reordered list would make a weaker key count as stronger.
risks.mitigation: The field doc comment and the athena.toml comment state the order and the 'ignored when earlier than the current model' rule. A config.rs table row with a reversed list pins the behavior, and a test pins REPO_CONFIG order (haiku before sonnet). The model part is a no-op in this repo.

risks.risk: The effect in this repo is effort only: sonnet is already the planner's model for a hard job, and Opus cannot be named because it may not produce (config.rs:650).
risks.mitigation: CHANGELOG and D179 say so. The drain.rs test asserts the effective difference is in effort (high to xhigh).

risks.risk: xhigh effort on revision calls may cost more or run longer. `planner_usd` stays 3.00 and `planner_timeout_s` 600 (athena.toml:209-216), so a call could hit its cap.
risks.mitigation: Caps are not changed; a timeout stops planning with the existing reason. Raising caps is out of scope. The change is reversible by deleting two keys.

risks.risk: `deny_unknown_fields` on Models could stop an older Athena binary from reading the new athena.toml.
risks.mitigation: A job reads its config from its own base commit, and the new binary lands with the change. Drain rebuilds Athena after landing its own code (D140).

risks.risk: Stripping the keys in `repo_with_config` could hide a regression where the keys leak into a test's config.
risks.mitigation: The new tests set the keys explicitly through the helper, and the drain.rs test reads athena.toml as it is.

risks.risk: The membership check after the family loop means a stray model with a family problem reports ModelFamily first.
risks.mitigation: Both are config refusals at load; the owner fixes them in turn. A config.rs test pins PlannerRevisionNotAllowed on an otherwise valid config.

demonstrations.method: A scripted job with [job_plan] on and max_rounds 3. The repository helper sets the keys to claude-sonnet-5-5 and xhigh. The planner queue is `[good_plan()]`. The critic queue is `[revising_critique(), accepting_critique()]`. A wrapper around `planning_script` records `(role, spec.model, spec.effort)`. The test reads the job's Planner invocation records and the `Lines` UI.
demonstrations.observes: Planner call 1 records the ordinary model (the reader's scripted producer model) and effort high. Planner call 2, after the critic's revise, records claude-sonnet-5-5 and xhigh. Both appear in the job's Planner invocation records. The critic calls keep their own model and effort. The job lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: With planning.rs unchanged, call 2 would record the ordinary model and high, and the assertions on call 2 and on the UI line would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::go` (via `athena.ask` then `athena.go`) with `Athena` built by `athena_with` and the `FakeAgentDriver` script injected, as `run_planned` does. `athena_with`, `planning_script`, `good_plan`, `revising_critique`, `accepting_critique`, `Lines` and `Records::load` exist (run/tests.rs:172, 190, 1193, 1140, 1173, 1166). Plan step 6 adds the settings-recording wrapper and the `repo_with_revision_keys` helper.

demonstrations.method: Three tests on the same seam. (a) Mechanical: planner queue `[bad_plan(), good_plan()]`, critic accepts. (b) Weaker keys: the scripted reader's producer_model is overridden to claude-sonnet-5-5, as `run_planned_behavior` mutates the reader output. Pair 1 is model haiku with effort medium. Pair 2 is model haiku with effort xhigh. The critic revises. (c) Both keys unset: planner queue `[bad_plan(), good_plan()]` and a revising critic over 3 rounds.
demonstrations.observes: (a) Planner calls are (ordinary, high) then (sonnet, xhigh), with no critic call between them, and the critic then runs once. (b) Pair 1: every planner call stays (sonnet, high). Pair 2: revision calls are (sonnet, xhigh), so only the effort part applies. (c) Every planner call across the mechanical pass and all 3 rounds is the same (ordinary, high).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the mechanical-pass condition, (a) records the ordinary setting on call 2. Without the no-weaker rule, (b) records (haiku, medium) on revision calls. Without the unset fallback, (c) fails when any call differs.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: `Athena::go`, `athena_with`, a `FakeAgentDriver` script wrapping `planning_script`. Step 6 adds the helpers. Existing tests that use `repo_with_config` run with the keys stripped, so they are unaffected.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in config.rs `mod tests` over `Config::parse` and `Config::reading_inputs` on `REPO_CONFIG`. (1) The keys parse as Some in REPO_CONFIG and as None once the two lines are stripped, and the stripped config loads. (2) A model outside producer_allowed (the verifier's Opus, or an unknown name) gives `ConfigError::PlannerRevisionNotAllowed`. Effort 'turbo' gives `ConfigError::Effort("planner_revision_effort", ..)`; the key is added to the loop of the existing effort test. (3) A table test of `planner_revision_setting`: stronger, equal and weaker for model and effort, unset, plus a row with producer_allowed reversed to [sonnet, haiku] showing a haiku-earlier/sonnet-earlier key is ignored exactly when it sits earlier in the list than the current model. (4) Changing hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort does not change the result. (5) `reading_inputs` is equal with and without the keys. Existing family tests are run too: `cargo test -p athena-data roles_without`.
